title: legal_pairs carries a per-pair row count that every table change corrects by hand
body:
`surface/dispatch-table.json` carries, in every `legal_pairs` entry, a field `n`: the number of rows in the table whose (`disposition`, `target.state`) pair is that entry's. `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/gen_dispatch_table.sh` refuses (its `PAIR_COUNT_STALE` arm) whenever an entry's `n` differs from the rows it counts, and refuses an entry with no `n` at all, so every row added, retired or re-paired forces a hand correction of the figure and a dated `census_note` line beside it. The notes show the figure has been corrected at every such change since the matrix landed, and ST0086's estate rows corrected it again on 2026-10-25 (ic, under vc's ruling, to keep the generator green inside a bank that is not the generator's).

That is a count written down and corrected rather than deleted, which the user-scope rule every session loads forbids: no count goes into a doc, a guard, a test or a constant, and a count already written down is deleted, never corrected. The property the arm was written for (a row's pair changing with no record of who chose it) is carried without a number: the pair-legality refusal (`PAIR_ILLEGAL`) and the retire and new-surface lockstep refusal beside it judge the relation itself, the row's own `basis` and `disposition_basis` say who chose its pair, and git history holds every change to it.

THE ASK: `n` goes from every `legal_pairs` entry and the `PAIR_COUNT_STALE` arm goes from the generator, with its mutation-proof comment block; the `census_note` lines lose their figures (a dated line may stay as history, but a line that exists only to carry a number goes); `surface/dispatch-table.md` re-renders; every other script under `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/` that reads `.n` (grep names `stale_at_check.sh`, `gen_reference.sh`, `implemented_check.sh`, `of_n_closes_over_examined.sh`, some of which read a different `n`) is checked before the field goes. The Rust side reads `legal_pairs` nowhere (only a doc comment in `dispatch.rs` names it), so no suite changes. Shell, S. After ST0086, not inside it.
